validity.recommendation: no change needed; optionally soften EndLocation from 'Gharo' to 'Bin Qasim/FJFC area' if the row is ever revisited for endpoint precision
validity.researcher_notes: gem.wiki returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch (Cloudflare) so no leads could be pulled from the sheet's own citation; wiki_citations.json is empty for this row per the scope note. Went straight to open-web/primary research. FOUND: SSGC's own published transmission-network table, 'Gas Transmission Capacities Utilization as on June 30, 2018' (ssgc.com.pk/web/?page_id=5597), lists under the 'Indus Left Bank Pipeline System (A1)' a line named exactly 'Loopline (Sind University to FJFC Offtake)' at 116 km, 24-inch diameter, 60 mmscfd rated capacity -- an exact match to GEM's LengthKnown=116.00 km, Diameter=24 in, Capacity=60.00 MMcf/d. This is a primary source (SSGC is both operator and the row's Owner1) and independently confirms the pipeline is real, transmission-class (not a gathering/feeder line -- it sits in SSGC's core Indus Left Bank trunk table alongside the Nawabshah-Karachi and Kadanwari-Malir-Karachi trunks), and matches on every numeric spec. SECOND, independent origin: a Pakistan Petroleum Information Service (PPIS) 'Energy Map 2013' (reproduced at pdfcoffee.com/ppis-energy-map-2013-a4-pdf-free.html; PPIS operates under the Directorate General of Petroleum Concessions, a separate origin from SSGC's own website) lists '24"x116KM, JAMSHORO-PAKLAND LOOPLINE YEAR 2005' -- same length (116 km) and diameter (24 in), same Jamshoro origin, built 2005, under a slightly different name (Pakland vs FJFC as the downstream endpoint reference). Two independent sources agreeing on length + diameter + Jamshoro origin + transmission-grade status = high confidence on existence, length, diameter, classification. Capacity (60 mmscfd) and Owner (SSGC 100%) rest on the single SSGC source only (medium). CAVEAT: neither source names the GEM EndLocation 'Gharo' verbatim -- SSGC calls the downstream point 'FJFC Offtake' (Fauji Jordan Fertilizer Co, now Fauji Fertilizer Bin Qasim Ltd, at Bin Qasim/Port Qasim) and PPIS calls it 'Pakland' (a Sales Meter Station also in the Bin Qasim/Karachi coastal industrial belt, per separate SSGC/press mentions of RLNG injection at SMS Pakland). Gharo is a real town on that same corridor (Thatta district, between Jamshoro and the Bin Qasim coast) so this reads as a plausible GEM-assigned nearest-named-place rather than an error, but the exact endpoint facility name in GEM's EndLocation field is not independently corroborated -- flagging as a caveat, not a concern. DUPLICATE CHECK against the 63-row roster: no other row matches this 116 km / 24-in / Jamshoro-origin profile -- P4014 (Nawabshah-Karachi, 290 km/16in), P4015 (Kadanwari-Malir-Karachi, 412 km/24-20in), P4017 (HQ2-Tando Adam, 81 km/24in), P4018 (Badin, 101 km/18in), and P4020 (Bajara-Karachi Loopline, 200 km/24in) are all distinct lines independently confirmed in the same two source tables/maps under their own names -- P4016 is not a relabel or segment double-count of any of them. Fuel=Gas and Status=operating are consistent with SSGC's own current network table (utility gas transmission line, actively tabulated as of the 2018 capacity-utilization snapshot) and the 2005-build/2013-map corroboration. No existence, classification, or duplicate concern found.

Gharo is a real Thatta-district town on that same Jamshoro-to-Bin Qasim corridor, so GEM's EndLocation is a plausible nearest-named-place rather than an error, but is not literally corroborated by either source -- medium tier on the endpoint specifically, high confidence on the corridor/start point.
